_: What the control room looks like (dev-docs/poltergeist/control-room.md, 3.5).
This file is data. tools/gen-control-room-look.py turns it into
tools/the-control-room-look-is-one-set.py is red when either is out of step.
Lengths are points, times are seconds. These are readings off the design, not off a product.
Every value names where it was read (`src`, a key of `sources`); a group's `_src` covers the
values in it that name none. A value the user has not ruled on carries `tentative`, with the
other candidate, so that ruling on it is one edit here and both hosts follow.
A colour is `#RRGGBB`, or `#RRGGBB@a` with a from 0 to 1.

sources.supervisor: the supervisor's ruling, not a design file
sources.undesigned: not in the design: chosen while building the mac list, to be ruled on
sources.v17-contrast: design v17, src/contrast.md (measured off the rendered pictures)

font._doc: Type sizes. Nothing is set smaller than `min`.

body.doc: Body text, tab titles, the terminal.

group_name.doc: A group's name in the list.

minutes.doc: How many minutes it has waited. Bold, so it counts as large text.

weight_emphasis.doc: The selected tab, a status word, a title.

weight_strong.doc: The selected group's name, the minutes.

line._doc: The only two widths there are.

stroke.doc: The plus and the cross; the rail of the time band.

window.doc: The system's; drawn as 14 in the design.

row.doc: 12 = 6 + 6: concentric with the panel through its padding.

supervisor_inner.doc: The terminal inside the supervisor's frame: 12 - 4.

window_edge.doc: From the window's edge to anything.

supervisor_bezel.doc: The supervisor's border, and its gap to the terminal inside.

terminal_text_inset.doc: Left and right of the terminal's text.

window_tab._doc: A window tab holds three things: close, title, one status glyph.

side_slot.doc: The width kept on each side, so the title stays centred.

working_glyph_shown.doc: Whether a working terminal's spinner is drawn on a window tab. Off, so that every glyph in the row of tabs is one to look at.

tentative.why: The design drew it; the supervisor chose not to. The user has not ruled.

row_height.doc: A group that is waiting for you: two lines.

quiet_row_height.doc: A group that needs nothing: one line.

time_lane_labelled_height.doc: A lane's height once it carries its group's name: 13 pt text does not fit the design's 12.

tentative.why: The design draws three unlabelled lanes 12 high and does not say which group each is. 12 is the design's height, with no label.

time_lane_label_width.doc: The column at a lane's left end that holds its group's name: twelve characters of the 13 pt monospaced face, which is the whole of most names. A longer one is cut at the end.

separator_space_above.doc: Below the last waiting row's own gap.

row_line2_height.doc: The glyph, the status word, the detail.

status_word_gap.doc: Between a glyph and its word.

pane._doc: The three frames a split can wear.

supervisor_floats.doc: It has a shadow; the other two do not.

stack_tab._doc: The tabs over a cell that holds several terminals.

inset.doc: From the content's left and right edges to a tab's body: corner 8 + straight 4 + arc 8. Also the terminal text's inset.

tentative.why: At 16 the arc's foot meets the end of the corner and the two read as one S.

reverse_arc_radius.doc: The arcs that join the current tab's foot to the content.

overlap_below.doc: How far the current tab's fill runs past its foot, to cover the strip's line.

status._doc: The four status glyphs and how they move. Nothing moves under Reduce Motion.

waiting_pulse_period.doc: Only the one that has waited longest pulses.

problem_shake_distance.doc: Left and right, once, on entering the state.

working_spin_steps.doc: It steps; it does not turn smoothly.

working_spoke_width.doc: One of the spinner's short lines, on the artboard.

working_spoke_inset.doc: From the artboard's edge to a line's outer end.

working_spoke_min_opacity.doc: The faintest line; the brightest is 1 and the rest step up to it.

done_unseen_dot.doc: The dot's diameter on the artboard: a size smaller than the other glyphs.

selection._doc: The selected row of the group list: a chip at rest, glass while it slides.

edge_band.doc: The width of the faint band just inside the chip's edge.

spring_damping.doc: Below 1, so it overshoots (about 4%) and settles.

tentative.why: Whether the chip overshoots at all has not been ruled on; 1 is critically damped.

lift_in.doc: How long the chip takes to lift when it starts to move.

lift_scale_window_tab.doc: The window tab's chip is the system's to draw; this is what the design hoped for.

stretch_along.doc: At most, with speed, along the direction of travel.

centre_zoom.doc: The middle of the chip while lifted.

refraction_shown.doc: Whether the chip's edge bends what is under it.

tentative.why: The other candidate keeps the lift and the slide and drops the refraction. Whether it can be done live is unverified.

seen_after.doc: How long a row stays selected, with the control room in front, before its group counts as seen.

tentative.why: 0 marks it seen the moment it is selected, so arrowing past a row would clear it.

refraction_strength_rest.doc: A fraction of the band's width; strongest at the edge, falling off as the square.

selection_tint.doc: How much white the chip mixes in, at rest.

selection_edge.doc: The band inside the edge: darker when negative, lighter when positive.

selection_shadow_blur.doc: As the design's animation takes it; its still pictures use about twice this as a CSS blur.

selection_halo_blur.doc: A second shadow with no offset.

window_base.doc: The window's ground. The design lays two faint blooms over it.

attention.doc: Blue, something for you: the glyph of waiting and of done-and-unseen.

attention_text.doc: The same blue as a word or a number.

problem.doc: Red, something is wrong: the glyph.

problem_text.doc: The same red as a word or a number. See `text_on` for where the word is not red.

side_panel_highlight.doc: A hairline along the top edge.

supervisor_edge_focused.doc: Light: the outer edge darkens. Dark: a ring is added just inside it.

surface_row.doc: Measured: an unselected row as it comes out over the panel. For contrast, not for painting.

surface_window_tab.doc: Measured: an unselected window tab on its track.

symbol._doc: The system symbols the glyphs are. Working is the system's progress spinner, which has no symbol name. `held` is the supervisor's ruling (the design says only `a pause glyph`).

_doc: Which colour a status word is written in, by the surface it sits on.
Dark red text does not reach 4.5 on the lighter dark surfaces, and lightening the red makes it
another colour. So there the word is written in the main text colour and the red is left to the
glyph and the minutes. That is the whole of this table, and the hosts read it rather than decide.

tentative.why: The other candidate accepts a contrast of about 3. The user has not ruled.

_doc: What is drawn on what, for the contrast report (`gen-control-room-look.py --contrast`).
`text` needs 4.5, `large` (20 pt bold) and `glyph` need 3. `problem_word` is the status word
